name: MonarchQueryBuilder
title: QueryBuilder
wrapsNative: Nested VStack groups, each with a segmented Picker for AND / OR; rules stacked vertically with Picker(.menu) for the field and the operator, and a TextField, DatePicker or Picker(.menu) for the value; Buttons with buttonStyle(.monarch()) to add and remove
summary: Builds a filter query from AND and OR groups of field, operator and value rules, nested up to a set depth, with validation and a matcher for previews.
whenToUse: For advanced search or segment definitions where people combine conditions with AND and OR, such as "status is open AND (amount is at least 500 OR flagged)".
whenNotToUse: For filters that simply combine with AND, use MonarchFacetedFilterPanel; for a few fixed filters, a Menu with a Picker; for a free-text search, .searchable.
api: MonarchQueryBuilder.init(query: Binding<MonarchQueryGroup>, fields: [MonarchConditionField], maxDepth: Int = 3, maxRulesPerGroup: Int = 20, showsErrors: Bool = false, labels: MonarchQueryBuilderLabels = MonarchQueryBuilderLabels(), makeID: @escaping @MainActor () -> String = { UUID().uuidString })
MonarchQueryGroup.init(id: String, combinator: MonarchQueryCombinator = .and, rules: [MonarchCondition] = [], groups: [MonarchQueryGroup] = [])
func MonarchQueryGroup.matches(_ values: [String: MonarchConditionValue], calendar: Calendar = .current) -> Bool
MonarchCondition.init(id: String, field: String, operator: MonarchConditionOperator, value: MonarchConditionValue = .none)
func MonarchCondition.matches(_ actual: MonarchConditionValue, calendar: Calendar = .current) -> Bool
MonarchConditionField.init(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchConditionFieldType, operators: [MonarchConditionOperator]? = nil, prompt: String? = nil)
enum MonarchConditionFieldType { case text, number, date, boolean, select([MonarchComboboxOption]) }
enum MonarchQueryCombinator: String { case and, or }

enum MonarchConditionOperator: String { case equals, notEquals, contains, notContains, greaterThan, atLeast, lessThan, atMost, before, after, isTrue, isFalse, isEmpty, isNotEmpty; var takesValue: Bool }
enum MonarchConditionValue { case none, text(String), number(Double?), date(Date?), boolean(Bool), option(String?); var isEmpty: Bool }
enum MonarchConditionProblem: String { case field, value, option }

options.name: query
options.description: The top group: a combinator, its rules and its nested groups.

options.name: fields
options.description: The fields a rule can test. The kind (text, number, date, boolean, select) decides the operators and the value input; operators narrows them.

options.name: maxDepth
options.description: How many levels of groups are allowed, counting the top group. 1 turns off nested groups.

options.name: maxRulesPerGroup
options.description: The most rules in one group; Add rule is replaced by a note at the limit.

options.name: showsErrors
options.description: Shows what is missing under each incomplete rule, with a danger border, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: group names, AND and OR, the spoken names of every control, operator names and problems.

options.name: makeID
options.description: Makes the id of a new rule or group.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the builder disables every menu, field and button and uses the disabled text role.

appearance: Nested groups have a subtle border and alternate the subtle and surface background roles so depth stays visible; rules are surface cards with a subtle border, or the danger strong border when they show a problem. The AND / OR switch and the menus are the system's controls; text uses the default and muted roles. The dark and high-contrast themes swap every role.
platformNotes: Each rule is a MonarchConditionRow, the row of MonarchConditionEditor, so the two components look and speak the same. The web QueryBuilder lays each group's rules out as a ConditionEditor row (field, operator and value side by side) and supports multi-select, tags, in and not-in values. On iOS each rule stacks vertically for a phone, field and operator are menu Pickers, and the value is a text field, a number field that parses in the current locale, a DatePicker (after Choose a date), or a menu of choices; in / not in, multi-select and tags are not offered (use several rules joined by OR). The web's number problem is the value problem here, because a number that does not parse is no number. There is no MonarchConditionEditor yet, so the rule row is part of this component. Focus after removing a group or rule is left to the system. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The builder is a container named "Query"; each group is a container named after it ("Top group", "Group 2.1") and its visible name has the header trait.
Each rule is a container named "Top group, rule 1"; its field menu, operator menu and value are named "Top group, rule 1 field", "… operator" and "… value".
The AND / OR switch is a segmented Picker named "Top group combinator", so VoiceOver reads the selected choice.
Remove buttons are icon-only with spoken names ("Remove top group, rule 1", "Remove group 2").
A shown problem is text with an icon, and the rule's hint reads it.
Every control has a touch target of at least 44 points and the text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Changing a rule's field resets its operator to the field's first and empties the value; changing the operator keeps the value when it still fits.
A stored operator the field does not offer stays at the top of the operator menu so it is not lost.
A new nested group starts with the opposite combinator of its parent.
matches(_:calendar:) treats an empty group as matching, compares text without case and dates by day in the given calendar; the server stays the authority.
A number field keeps what is typed while it is not a number and stores nil until it parses.
